post.caption:
A day on Earth is getting longer. Not by much, but it never resets. The Moon's pull acts like a brake on Earth's spin, so the day lengthens and the Moon drifts a little farther away every year. We know it from growth rings in ancient coral. A dinosaur's day was only twenty three hours.
